meta.description: Use when working directly with the `esm` Python SDK, ESM3 or ESMC model IDs, Forge/Biohub inference clients, or ESMFold2 folding workflows.

scientific_integrity.detail: Accurate representation of ESM3/ESMC protein language models based on published Science paper (Hayes et al., 2025) and official SDK

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for protein engineering with explicit Responsible Biodesign Framework and biosafety considerations

methodological_ground.detail: Based on established protein language models with peer-reviewed foundation (ESM3 in Science 2025) and validated model architectures

code_usability.detail: All code examples are syntactically correct with proper imports and SDK usage patterns

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive coverage of ESM capabilities including ESM3 generation, ESMC embeddings, structure prediction, inverse folding, function conditioning, with excellent reference organization

reliability.note: Good best practices for production deployment with error handling, retry logic, and rate limiting; minor: could expand troubleshooting for common API errors

performance_context.note: Well-organized documentation (335 lines) with clear model selection guide, 5 comprehensive reference files, and workflow patterns

agent_usability.note: Excellent capability organization with 'When to use' sections for each major function; clear model selection criteria; comprehensive workflows reference

human_usability.note: Clear installation with Flash Attention optimization; authentication guidance with environment variable pattern; model selection guide with local vs Forge tradeoffs

security.note: Good credential handling with ESM_API_KEY pattern and explicit token protection rules; endpoint validation mentioned; minor: could add more explicit biosafety guidelines for novel protein designs

maintainability.note: Excellent structure with version 1.1, clear license (MIT), 5 comprehensive references, version pinning (esm 3.2.3, Python >=3.12,<3.13), and authoritative resource links

agent_specific.note: Strong composability with allowed-tools and async batch processing patterns; clear local vs Forge API distinction; minor: output format schemas not fully specified for embeddings/coordinates

key_strengths: Exceptional coverage of multimodal protein language models with clear distinctions between generative (ESM3) and embedding (ESMC) workflows
Outstanding model selection guidance with local vs Forge tradeoffs, model sizes, and selection criteria mapped to use cases
Excellent responsible use framework with explicit references to Responsible Biodesign and biosafety considerations for novel protein designs
Strong API design consistency with unified interface between local and hosted models (same generate/encode methods)
Comprehensive chain-of-thought generation workflow demonstrating iterative refinement across structure/sequence/function tracks

recommendations.title: Add async error handling patterns for batch processing
recommendations.problem: Async batch processing shown but error handling in async context not demonstrated
recommendations.root_cause: Best practices mention retry logic but no code example for async failure handling
recommendations.fix: Add example with try/except in async function, asyncio.TimeoutError handling, and retry with exponential backoff for Forge API failures

recommendations.title: Add rate limiting implementation example
recommendations.problem: Best practices recommend rate limiting but no implementation guidance
recommendations.root_cause: Production deployment advice lacks concrete rate limiting pattern
recommendations.fix: Add example using asyncio.Semaphore for concurrent request limiting or reference to Forge API rate limit headers

recommendations.title: Expand biosafety guidelines for specific protein classes
recommendations.problem: Responsible use section provides framework links but limited inline guidance
recommendations.root_cause: Security section defers to external policies without skill-specific warnings
recommendations.fix: Add inline note: 'Exercise caution when designing proteins with potential pathogenic, toxic, or dual-use capabilities; consult institutional biosafety review before experimental validation'
